[json-extracted] The browser package changefile comment does not include the required linked PR number. The documented changefile convention requires every change message to end with a description followed by a linked PR number. Without it, release notes lose their required traceability to the implementation review. Suggestion: Append `[#8819](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-js/pull/8819)` to the comment.

[json-extracted] The new public PCA token-cache operation lacks a test that exercises the public `pca.getTokenCache().loadDpopNonce()` path. The added cache tests validate `BrowserCacheManager` directly, while the public API is implemented through a new `TokenCache` wrapper and controller delegation. A regression in PCA-to-controller-to-cache wiring would not be detected by the current tests. Suggestion: Add a browser unit test that creates and initializes a `PublicClientApplication`, calls `getTokenCache().loadDpopNonce(...)`, and verifies the expected nonce is available through the bound browser cache manager.

_Merged from: missing-public-dpop-nonce-documentation_

[json-extracted] clearDpopNonces silently ignores removal failures, while the subsequent full-cache cleanup deliberately skips every DPoP nonce key. If storage removeItem throws, clearDpopNonces leaves the nonce persisted but reports success. BrowserCacheManager.clear then encounters that same key and returns early because parseDpopNonceCacheKey succeeds, so logout or clearCache can complete with a still-loadable stale nonce. This is reproducible with a supported custom IWindowStorage implementation and can also occur when browser storage operations fail. Suggestion: Continue attempting all nonce removals but retain and propagate a sanitized failure afterward, or have clear() retry current-client DPoP keys instead of unconditionally skipping them. Add coverage where removeItem fails and verify clearing does not report success while the nonce remains.

_Flagged by: review-logic, review-fresh-eyes_

_Merged from: logout-can-leave-dpop-nonces_

[json-extracted] A delayed nonce write validates all retained entries using the delayed entity's older timestamp, causing newer nonces for other origins to be classified as future-dated and deleted. The write queue is shared only within one JavaScript realm. If another tab writes origin B at time T2 while an origin A write created at T1 is awaiting hashing, the T1 write can resume later and call getDpopNonceEntries(nonceType, T1). The valid origin-B entry has lastUpdatedAt T2, so isDpopNonceEntityValid rejects it as future-dated and the enumeration removes it. The same-origin freshness check does not protect entries under different cache keys. Suggestion: Use the actual current time when validating retained entries during cleanup, rather than entity.lastUpdatedAt. Keep insertion ordering and eviction comparisons separate from entity-validity time, and add a test with an older delayed write and a newer nonce under a different origin.

_Flagged by: review-logic, review-fresh-eyes_

_Merged from: older-write-purges-newer-origins_

[json-extracted] The new getTokenCache method is added only to the concrete PublicClientApplication class and not to IPublicClientApplication. createStandardPublicClientApplication and createNestablePublicClientApplication both return Promise<IPublicClientApplication>, and wrapper libraries also expose instances through that interface. Consumers using those supported paths therefore get a TypeScript error when calling getTokenCache, making the new public nonce-loading API inaccessible despite the runtime object implementing it. Suggestion: Add getTokenCache(): ITokenCache to IPublicClientApplication, implement the corresponding stub behavior, and update the API review so the method is available through factory and wrapper return types.

_Flagged by: review-logic, review-fresh-eyes_

_Merged from: missing-public-dpop-nonce-documentation_
The new public DPoP nonce cache API has no corresponding workflow documentation, and an existing migration guide contradicts the changed API surface.

[json-extracted] The PR introduces the public ITokenCache.loadDpopNonce API without updating msal-browser documentation. The API is exported and exposed from PublicClientApplication, but no documentation describes its resource-origin scoping, input constraints, persistence lifecycle, or error behavior. Consumers therefore have no supported usage guidance for the new public surface. Suggestion: Add msal-browser documentation for getTokenCache().loadDpopNonce(), including HTTPS resource URI requirements, opaque nonce handling, cache-location behavior, and nonce removal during logout or cache clearing.

[json-extracted] getTokenCache() is added only to the PublicClientApplication class, not to the public IPublicClientApplication interface returned and consumed by MSAL factory and wrapper APIs. Consumers whose PCA is typed as IPublicClientApplication cannot call the newly documented getTokenCache(). This makes the advertised public DPoP nonce deposit API unavailable through the library's primary public abstraction, and leaves stubbed implementations without the member. Suggestion: Add getTokenCache(): ITokenCache to IPublicClientApplication, import the interface as a type there, and add a matching deterministic stub implementation to stubbedPublicClientApplication. Add coverage using a PCA value typed as IPublicClientApplication.

[json-extracted] Existing nonce entries are removed before the replacement write is known to succeed. At the capacity boundary, a non-quota setItem failure loses the oldest valid nonce even though no new value was stored. Under unresolved quota pressure, the retry loop can remove every nonce and still throw, leaving the cache unnecessarily empty. Suggestion: Avoid destructive pre-eviction for non-quota failures and preserve or restore removed entries when the new value cannot be persisted.

[json-extracted] The new public cache operation has no performance measurement or cache success/failure telemetry. Persistence failures, quota recovery, and invalid challenge values affect DPoP reliability but are currently invisible to the library's performance telemetry, preventing diagnosis of repeated nonce challenges in production. Suggestion: Wrap the operation with the repository's performance instrumentation, include a correlation ID, and record sanitized cache outcome fields without logging the nonce.

[json-extracted] loadDpopNonce persists the resource-server nonce, but no production code reads getDpopNonce when generating a subsequent DPoP proof. After a resource server returns a DPoP-Nonce challenge, an application can call this new API and retry token acquisition, but the generated proof still omits the stored nonce. The retry therefore receives the same challenge again, making the public persistence API behaviorally ineffective. Suggestion: Read the cached resource-server nonce during DPoP resource-proof generation and pass it into the proof parameters. Add a challenge-load-reacquire test that asserts the resulting proof contains the nonce.

[json-extracted] Nonce write serialization is held only in an in-memory WeakMap and does not coordinate localStorage writes across tabs. Separate browsing contexts have separate WeakMaps but share the same localStorage. Concurrent challenge responses can both read the old value and then overwrite each other; equal-millisecond timestamps are especially vulnerable because the newer-value guard only rejects strictly older writes. Suggestion: Add cross-context conflict handling, such as a storage-backed version/order check immediately before committing, and cover concurrent localStorage writers from separate contexts.
